samples.summary: The new `clampDecimals` guard only covers the render path; the step/write path still reads an untrusted stored `dp` unclamped
samples.evidence: `clampDecimals` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/format.ts:22) is introduced precisely because "a `dp` can come from anywhere a style can — an imported `.xlsx`, a collaborator's document". But the write path never passes through it: `getActiveDecimalState` returns `style.dp` raw (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4184), `changeDecimals` does arithmetic on that raw value (`Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)`, sheet.ts:4202) and then stores the result (`setRangeStyle({ dp: target })`, sheet.ts:4236) and also uses it as the unset match value (`{ dp, nf }`, sheet.ts:4230). A stored non-integer/non-number `dp` therefore round-trips back into the shared document: a `dp` of `"3"` from a peer or import makes `dp + delta` string-concatenate to `"31"`, which is then written as the new `dp`; a fractional `dp` of 2.5 is stored as 3.5. `getActiveDecimalPlaces` (sheet.ts:4156) likewise hands `style?.dp ?? 2` to callers unclamped. Fix belongs on the new code: clamp in `getActiveDecimalState`/`changeDecimals` before stepping, not only inside `formatValue`.

samples.summary: `renderedDecimals` hardcodes 2 decimals for a `dp`-less currency format, contradicting `formatValue`'s currency branch for non-2-digit currencies (KRW, JPY, KWD)
samples.evidence: `renderedDecimals` returns `clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2)` for every numeric format (format.ts:160), but `formatValue` deliberately omits the fraction-digit options for currency when `dp === undefined` (format.ts:198-203) so Intl applies the *currency's own* default: 0 for KRW/JPY, 3 for KWD. `resolveCurrencyForLocale` maps KR→KRW and JP→JPY (packages/sheets/src/model/core/locale.ts:47,49), so this is a routine document, not an exotic one. `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4263) now decides the Decrease no-op through `renderedDecimals`, so a KRW/JPY currency cell that actually renders 0 decimals reports 2, the whole-selection no-op guard is defeated, and Decrease writes an explicit `{dp: 0}` residue onto neighbours that had no style at all — the exact residue the feature exists to avoid. docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:257 repeats the same wrong assumption ("an absent `dp` means the *format's* default of 2").

But the write path never passes through it: `getActiveDecimalState` returns `style.dp` raw (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4184), `changeDecimals` does arithmetic on that raw value (`Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)`, sheet.ts:4202) and then stores the result (`setRangeStyle({ dp: target })`, sheet.ts:4236) and also uses it as the unset match value (`{ dp, nf }`, sheet.ts:4230). verdict.reason: The code is present exactly where claimed. clampDecimals (format.ts:22-30) is applied only on the render side (format.ts:160, format.ts:182), while the mutation path reads the stored dp raw (sheet.ts:4183-4184), steps it (sheet.ts:4202), uses it as the unset match value (sheet.ts:4229-4231) and persists the result (sheet.ts:4236-4240) with no clamping. The path is reachable from the UI via Spreadsheet.increaseDecimals/decreaseDecimals (spreadsheet.ts:536, :546), and untrusted dp genuinely reaches storage (xlsx-styles.ts:413 derives dp from an imported format code; peer style writes do the same). A stored NaN or non-numeric dp yields stepped = NaN, which fails the `stepped < 0` branch and is written back as `dp: NaN`; a fractional 2.5 is stored as 3.5. Both violate the `dp: number` (non-negative integer) invariant other consumers rely on (pivot/parse.ts:19, sheet-view.tsx:62) and round-trip into the shared document. Two sub-claims are wrong but do not carry the finding: `Math.min("31", 20)` coerces, so a string dp is never stored as "31" (it degrades to NaN instead), and getActiveDecimalPlaces (sheet.ts:4154-4157) has no callers repo-wide. I considered `already-guarded` because every render consumer does pass through clampDecimals (sheet.ts:972, sheet.ts:4734, gridcanvas.ts:1596, :1777, chart-utils.ts:364, bridge.ts:319) so no Intl RangeError escapes — but that guards reads, not the unguarded write, so the invariant violation stands.

verdict.reason: All cited code is present as described. format.ts:160 returns clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2) for every non-plain/non-date format, while formatValue's currency branch (format.ts:198-203) omits fraction-digit options when dp is undefined, letting Intl apply the currency's own default (0 for JPY/KRW, 3 for KWD). locale.ts:47,49,50 maps JP/KR/KW to those currencies and is the default currency source at format.ts:184; render paths pass currency: style?.cu (sheet.ts:972, sheet.ts:4734, view/gridcanvas.ts:1596), so the 0-decimal currency render is reachable both via explicit cu and via a JP/KR system locale. selectionRendersAt (sheet.ts:4252-4269) decides the Decrease no-op solely through renderedDecimals at sheet.ts:4263, and changeDecimals gates on it at sheet.ts:4203; a currency cell truly rendering 0 decimals reports 2, so the no-op guard is defeated and control falls to setRangeStyle({dp: 0}) at sheet.ts:4236-4240, writing the explicit-dp residue on previously style-free neighbours that the rule exists to avoid (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:283-284). docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:257-258 repeats the same wrong assumption. It is in this lens's lane rather than pure correctness: it is a cross-module invariant (renderedDecimals must agree with what formatValue paints) whose breakage can only be established by reading formatValue's pre-existing currency contract and the locale currency table outside the changed logic, and it leaves the sheet.ts consumer silently wrong. No guard elsewhere excludes non-2-digit currencies.
